newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO TAKES GOLD AS URMANOV WITHDRAWS.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO TAKES GOLD AS URMANOV WITHDRAWS.

text.p: Canada's Elvis Stojko produced his spectacular trademark, a quadruple-triple jump combination, as he recaptured the men's world figure skating title on Thursday.
His task, however, was made simpler by the withdrawal through injury of Olympic champion Alexei Urmanov.
The Russian, who led after Wednesday's short programme and was favourite to take the title, pulled out with a groin injury after warming up with just the last group of skaters to go.
His withdrawal left Stojko with a virtual open door to walk through to the title he won in 1994 and 1995 although he still had to contend with the defending champion Todd Eldredge.
But the 25-year-old American had nothing to match Stojko's pyrotechnics and he fluffed two jumps late in his programme, singling out of a triple axel and falling on a double axel.
There were also a couple of scratchy landings in Stojko's programme to music from the movie "Dragonheart" but an Italian judge gave him a perfect 6.0 for technique while the others awarded him 5.9.
He had one score of 5.9 for artistry, six of 5.8 and two of 5.6 and won the free skating on the cards of eight of the nine judges.
That was enough to give him first place after both he and Eldredge totalled 3.0 factored placements based on positions in the short and long programmes.
Stojko first produced the quadruple toe loop-triple toe loop combination as he won the Champions Series final in Hamilton, Ontario, earlier this month.
After his fourth place finish -- despite a faultless performance -- in the short programme, he knew he needed to produce it again - and he did.
Russian teenager Alexei Yagudin captured third place with Viacheslav Zagorodniuk of Ukraine fourth after both made uncharacteristic jumping errors.
Russian Ilya Kulik had a bad night and dropped from third to fifth with the sixth best free programme.

Earlier on Friday, Russians Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov strengthened their lead in the ice dance by winning the tango, with teammates Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov remaining second and Canadians Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz third.
